I've changed the stand so the phone's center of mass lands over the middle of the base, and saved it to `/lab/work/stand.solidcraft` and exported `/lab/work/stand.stl` (stand only). I worked the balance out by hand from the slot geometry. I didn't put a phone body in the model, and I didn't measure the final stand's own center of mass.

**What was wrong:** the original slot leaned the phone toward the front edge. By my calculation its center of mass sat about 6 mm in front of the base, with the base spanning 0 to 60 mm front to back. So the phone would have tipped forward.

**What I changed (parameters):**
- **`back_angle`:** 70° → 110°, which mirrors the lean so the phone now leans toward the back of the stand. The angle from horizontal is still 70°.
- **`stand_depth`:** 60 → 90 mm. At 60 mm the slot would have had to sit at the very front edge to balance.
- **`front_lip`:** 15 → 14.65 mm, the value that puts the center of mass exactly at the middle.
- **`slot_floor`:** 8 → 10 mm. The flipped slot floor tilts down toward the back and would otherwise have left only about 4.6 mm of material underneath.

**Numbers I relied on:**
- The phone is 150 mm long, 9 mm thick and 210 g, and leans at 70° from horizontal.
- The slot is 10 mm wide (9 mm phone plus 1 mm clearance) and 25 mm deep along its axis, so the phone seats on a floor perpendicular to its length.
- The slot floor's midpoint, where the phone's bottom edge sits, is at y = 14.65 + 4.70 = 19.35 mm.
- The phone's center of mass is 75 mm along its length from the bottom edge, which shifts it back by 75 × cos 70° = 25.65 mm. That puts it at y = 19.35 + 25.65 = 45.0 mm, which is half of the 90 mm depth.
- Its height there is about 77 mm above the base.
- Side to side, the 72 mm phone sits in the middle of the 80 mm width, so it is also centered in x.

I didn't change the slot's 25 mm depth along its axis, so the phone is held only about 25 mm up its length.
